# Problem Index {#problem-index}

This index helps you find problems by LeetCode ID, difficulty, chapter, or platform.

```{r index-setup, include=FALSE}
# Problem database - loaded from CSV file
library(knitr)

# Load all problems from CSV file (105 currently in book)
problems <- read.csv("problems_data.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Ensure techniques column exists for older CSVs
if (!"techniques" %in% names(problems)) {
  problems$techniques <- ""
}

# Normalize missing techniques to empty strings for grepl
problems$techniques[is.na(problems$techniques)] <- ""

# Convert "NA" strings to actual NA values
problems$problem_id[problems$problem_id == "NA"] <- NA
problems$problem_id <- as.numeric(problems$problem_id)

# Add platform priority for sorting (LeetCode=1, HackerRank=2, Firecode=3, Others=4)
platform_order <- c(LeetCode = 1, HackerRank = 2, Firecode = 3, Other = 4, Interview = 4)
problems$platform_priority <- platform_order[problems$platform]
problems$platform_priority[is.na(problems$platform_priority)] <- max(platform_order) + 1

# Add HTML links for clickable problem titles
problems$html_link <- paste0("[", problems$title, "](", problems$anchor, ".html)")

technique_matches <- function(technique) {
  pattern <- paste0("(^|,\\s*)", technique, "(,|$)")
  problems[grepl(pattern, problems$techniques, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
}

render_technique_table <- function(technique) {
  matches <- technique_matches(technique)
  if (nrow(matches) == 0) {
    cat("*No problems using this technique yet.*\n")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  matches <- matches[order(matches$platform_priority, matches$problem_id, na.last = TRUE), ]
  matches$display_id <- ifelse(is.na(matches$problem_id), "-", as.character(matches$problem_id))
  matches$problem_link <- paste0("[", matches$title, "](", matches$anchor, ".html)")
  kable(matches[, c("platform", "display_id", "problem_link", "difficulty", "chapter")],
        col.names = c("Platform", "ID", "Problem", "Difficulty", "Chapter"),
        row.names = FALSE)
}
```

---

## Quick Lookup by Problem ID

Browse problems by platform, sorted by problem ID (numeric when present, otherwise by title):

```{r lookup-by-id, echo=FALSE, results='asis'}
platforms <- c("LeetCode", "HackerRank", "Firecode", "Other", "Interview")

for (p in platforms) {
  cat(paste0("### ", p, "\n\n"))
  df <- problems[problems$platform == p, ]
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    cat(paste0("*No problems for ", p, " yet.*\n\n"))
    next
  }
  df$problem_id_num <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(df$problem_id))
  df <- df[order(is.na(df$problem_id_num), df$problem_id_num, df$title, na.last = TRUE), ]
  df$display_id <- ifelse(is.na(df$problem_id_num), "-", as.character(df$problem_id))
  df$problem_link <- paste0("[", df$title, "](", df$anchor, ".html)")
  print(kable(df[, c("display_id", "problem_link", "difficulty", "chapter")],
              col.names = c("ID", "Problem", "Difficulty", "Chapter"),
              row.names = FALSE))
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

## Lookup by Chapter

```{r by-chapter, echo=FALSE}
# Create platform priority for sorting (LeetCode=1, HackerRank=2, Firecode=3, Others=4)
platform_order <- c(LeetCode = 1, HackerRank = 2, Firecode = 3, Other = 4, Interview = 4)
problems$platform_priority <- platform_order[problems$platform]
problems$platform_priority[is.na(problems$platform_priority)] <- max(platform_order) + 1

# Sort by chapter, then platform priority, then problem_id (NA last)
by_chapter <- problems[order(problems$chapter_num, problems$platform_priority, problems$problem_id, na.last = TRUE), ]
by_chapter$display_id <- ifelse(is.na(by_chapter$problem_id), "-", as.character(by_chapter$problem_id))
by_chapter$problem_link <- paste0("[", by_chapter$title, "](", by_chapter$anchor, ".html)")
kable(by_chapter[, c("chapter", "problem_link", "platform", "display_id", "difficulty")],
      col.names = c("Chapter", "Problem", "Platform", "Problem ID", "Difficulty"),
      row.names = FALSE)
```

## Lookup by Technique

This index helps you find problems by technique. It focuses on uncommon or specialized algorithms and data structures; common techniques like arrays, recursion, and basic iteration are not included since they appear in nearly every problem. Links jump to the detailed explanations in [Common Strategies](#common-strategies) and the [Glossary](#intro).

## Lookup by Study Plan

### Blind 75

```{r blind-75, echo=FALSE}
blind75 <- problems[grepl("Blind 75", problems$tags, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
cat(sprintf("*Progress: %d / 75 problems.*\n\n", nrow(blind75)))
if(nrow(blind75) > 0) {
  # Sort by platform priority, then problem_id
  blind75 <- blind75[order(blind75$platform_priority, blind75$problem_id, na.last = TRUE), ]
  blind75$display_id <- ifelse(is.na(blind75$problem_id), "-", as.character(blind75$problem_id))
  blind75$problem_link <- paste0("[", blind75$title, "](", blind75$anchor, ".html)")
  kable(blind75[, c("platform", "display_id", "problem_link", "difficulty", "chapter")],
        col.names = c("Platform", "ID", "Problem", "Difficulty", "Chapter"),
        row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  cat("*No problems tagged as Blind 75 yet. Tags will be populated by Codex.*\n")
}
```

## Lookup by Company

```{r company-tags, echo=FALSE}
# Extract all unique company tags from the tags column
# Common companies to check for
companies <- c("Google", "Amazon", "Meta", "Microsoft", "Apple", "Bloomberg", "Adobe", "Uber", "Netflix", "Facebook")

# Function to display problems for a company
show_company_problems <- function(company_name) {
  company_problems <- problems[grepl(company_name, problems$tags, ignore.case = TRUE), ]
  if(nrow(company_problems) > 0) {
    # Sort by platform priority, then problem_id
    company_problems <- company_problems[order(company_problems$platform_priority, company_problems$problem_id, na.last = TRUE), ]
    company_problems$display_id <- ifelse(is.na(company_problems$problem_id), "-", as.character(company_problems$problem_id))
    company_problems$problem_link <- paste0("[", company_problems$title, "](", company_problems$anchor, ".html)")
    cat(paste0("\n### ", company_name, " (", nrow(company_problems), " problems)\n\n"))
    print(kable(company_problems[, c("platform", "display_id", "problem_link", "difficulty", "chapter")],
          col.names = c("Platform", "ID", "Problem", "Difficulty", "Chapter"),
          row.names = FALSE))
  }
}

# Check if any company tags exist
has_company_tags <- any(sapply(companies, function(c) any(grepl(c, problems$tags, ignore.case = TRUE))))

if(has_company_tags) {
  for(company in companies) {
    show_company_problems(company)
  }
} else {
  cat("*No company tags found yet. Tags will be populated by Codex.*\n\nOnce populated, this section will show problems grouped by company (Google, Amazon, Meta, etc.).\n")
}
```

## How to Update This Index

When you add a new problem to the book:

1. Open [problems_data.csv](problems_data.csv) in a spreadsheet or text editor
2. Add a new row with: `title,platform,problem_id,difficulty,chapter,chapter_num,anchor,tags,techniques`
3. Use comma-separated technique anchors in the `techniques` column and wrap the value in quotes when it contains commas (example: `dp-tabulation, backtracking-choose-explore-unchoose-pattern`)
4. Rebuild the book with `sh build.sh`
5. All lookup tables will automatically update!

### Example CSV Entry

```
Your New Problem,LeetCode,9999,Medium,Array,02,new-problem,"Google, Amazon, Top 100 Liked, Blind 75","dp-tabulation, hash-table"
```

### Tags Format

The `tags` field supports comma-separated values for:
- **Company names**: Google, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft, Apple, Bloomberg, Adobe, Uber, Netflix
- **Study plans**: Top 100 Liked, Blind 75, NeetCode 150

Use quotes around the tags value if it contains commas.

---

### Techniques Format

The `techniques` field supports comma-separated technique anchor IDs for:
- **Dynamic Programming**: `dp-memoization`, `dp-tabulation`, `dp-unbounded-knapsack`, `kadanes-algorithm`
- **Backtracking**: `backtracking-choose-explore-unchoose-pattern`, `backtracking-pass-by-value-pattern`, `backtracking-mark-unmark-pattern`
- **Two Pointer**: `two-pointer`, `sliding-window`
- **Data Structures**: `stack`, `queue`, `heap`, `hash-table`, `bst`, `trie`, `linked-list`, `array`
- **Searching**: `dfs`, `bfs`, `binary-search`
- **Graph Traversal**: `undirected-graph-dfs`, `undirected-graph-bfs`, `dag-dfs`, `dag-bfs`
- **Sorting**: `sorting-bubble-sort`, `sorting-insertion-sort`, `sorting-merge-sort`, `sorting-quick-sort`, `sorting-topological-sort`
- **Statistical Sampling**: `rejection-sampling`, `reservoir-sampling`
- **Paradigms**: `greedy`, `dnc`, `recursion`
- **Matrix**: `matrix-traversal`, `matrix-manipulation`
- **Advanced**: `bitwise`, `simulation`, `probability`, `minimax`

Use quotes around the techniques value if it contains commas.

Cross-reference to technique explanations:
- Detailed techniques: [Common Strategies](#common-strategies)
- Quick reference: [Glossary](#intro)

## Summary Statistics

```{r stats, echo=FALSE}
cat("**Total Problems:**", nrow(problems), "\n\n")
cat("**By Difficulty:**\n")
cat("- Easy:", sum(problems$difficulty == "Easy"), "\n")
cat("- Medium:", sum(problems$difficulty == "Medium"), "\n")
cat("- Hard:", sum(problems$difficulty == "Hard"), "\n")
cat("- Unclassified:", sum(problems$difficulty == "Unclassified"), "\n\n")
cat("**By Platform:**\n")
for(p in unique(problems$platform)) {
  cat("-", p, ":", sum(problems$platform == p), "\n")
}
```
